Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral lateral displacement of the paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) in the lower posterior mediastinum without evidence of vertebral destruction or respiratory symptoms. This specific radiographic finding, combined with the patient's age and back pain, is most characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma presenting as a paravertebral mass, whereas neurogenic tumors are typically unilateral and extramedullary hematopoiesis is associated with severe anemia.
